description.summary: Tools for the PAM configuration common to all services
description.p: pam-auth-update writes the files /etc/pam.d/common-auth, common-account, common-password, common-session and common-session-noninteractive, which the PAM configuration of every service includes. What goes into them comes from profiles in /usr/share/pam-configs, which packages with a PAM module bring along. The package has the profile for the traditional Unix authentication with /etc/shadow. The program is a rewrite in shell of the one in Debian and takes the profiles of Debian packages as they are.

The package also has pam-securetty. "pam-securetty enable" restricts logins of root to the consoles it finds on the machine, by writing /etc/securetty and adding pam_securetty to the PAM configuration of login. "pam-securetty disable" takes that away again. Nothing of it is active unless it is enabled.

maintainer-scripts.postinst: # Writes /etc/pam.d/common-*. Files that were changed by hand are left # alone, the program says so and that is no failure. "$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX/sbin/pam-auth-update" --package
